raw_request: Maintain agent-memory as an independent, agent-neutral memory implementation with an OpenCode adapter, current AppSDK 0.1.6 governance, and preserved project memory.
understood_objective: Keep one Rust owner for memory admission, pending state, organization, persistence, recall, and recovery; expose it through a thin typed bridge and OpenCode adapter; verify changes through mapped tests, canonical build, and real host replay when runtime behavior changes.
acceptance_criteria: agent-memory remains an independent repository with clean owner-worktree development and protected mainline integration.
Rust Core remains the sole owner of memory semantics, persistence, organization, recall, and recovery.
OpenCode and future host adapters translate typed events without duplicating Core semantics or mixing control truth into business payloads.
Missing or malformed memory never changes parent agent output semantics; valid recognizable entries are admitted and invalid parts remain explicit diagnostics.
Pending, immutable knowledge, organization delta, epoch promotion, persistence, reopen, and recovery retain positive and negative regression coverage.
AppSDK 0.1.6 verify and compile use current project-owned module, function, and verification bindings without legacy migration records.
non_goals: Restoring DSH as the active host contract.
Owning agent-tui or another sibling repository.
Duplicating Rust memory semantics in TypeScript adapters.
Treating loader health or static tests alone as deployed memory behavior evidence.
assumptions: OpenCode remains the current primary host adapter.
The Rust JSONL bridge remains the canonical process boundary for the TypeScript adapter.
